integers, let a group G satisfy condition Ck,n if every k-generated subgroup of G is
finite of order at most n.
     a) Does there exist k ⩾ 2 such that for any n all groups with condition Ck,n are
locally finite?
    b) In particular, is it true that for any n the condition C2,n implies local finiteness?
     c) Find possibly more pairs (k, n) for which groups with condition Ck,n are locally
finite. (For example, all groups with condition C2,20 are metabelian, and therefore
locally finite.)                                                         A. Yu. Olshanskii

20.71. (J. Lauri). A card of a finite simple undirected graph G of order n = |V (G)|
is an induced subgraph of order n − 1. For a connected graph G with k isomorphism
types of cards, can Aut(G) have more than k orbits on the vertex set V (G)
    a) for k = 2?
    b) for k = 3?
   ∗ c) for k = 4?
    If a graph G has k isomorphism types of cards, then the group Aut(G) of auto-
morphisms of G has obviously at least k orbits on V (G). It is known that if all cards
are mutually isomorphic, then Aut(G) is transitive on V (G). Examples are known of
graphs G with 5 isomorphism types of cards for which Aut(G) has 6 orbits on V (G),
and of graphs with 6 isomorphism types for which Aut(G) has 7 orbits on V (G).
                                                                      V. Pannone
  ∗ c) Yes, it can for k = 4 (J. Prajapati, Preprint, 2026, https://github.com/
infinityscroll/kourovka-20-71).

(2011), 99–103); when m is square-free (I. M. Isaacs, Arch. Math., 97 (2011), 499–

D such that any n elements of D generate an X-subgroup, whereas ⟨D⟩ ∈      / X.

groups, homomorphic images, and extensions. A subgroup H of a finite group G is
said to be X-submaximal if there exists an embedding of G into a group G∗ such that
G is subnormal in G∗ and H coincides with the intersection of G and an X-maximal
subgroup of G∗ . Suppose that all X-submaximal subgroups of a characteristic sub-
group N of a finite group G are conjugate in N . Does it follow that HN/N is an
X-submaximal subgroup of G/N for every X-submaximal subgroup H of G?

a minimal generating system of F that contains ω, almost primitive if it is prim-
itive in each finitely generated proper subgroup of F containing ω, tame almost
primitive if, whenever ω α is contained in a subgroup H of F with α ⩾ 1 mini-
mal, either ω α is primitive in H or the index of H in F is just α. In (B. Fine,
A. Moldenhauer, G. Rosenberger, L. Wienke, Topics in Infinite Group Theory: Nielsen
Methods, Covering Spaces, and Hyperbolic Groups, De Gruyter, Berlin, 2021) it is

group on c1 , . . . , cp with p ⩾ 2.

product uv in the free group on a1 , b1 , . . . , ag , bg , c1 , . . . , cp ?

nite subset E(g) of G such that for every x ∈ G all sufficiently long commutators

**Kourovka 19th/20th issue: computationally attackable candidates (sorted by score)**

Score 4
- **19.108** (Wilde): P a p-group, p odd, χ∈Irr(P), χ(x)≠0 ⇒ o(x) | |P|/χ(1)². Attack: exhaust SmallGroups of order p^6, p^7 (p=3,5,7; 504/9310, 684/34297, 860/860052 groups; 3^8 if time) — for each χ and class rep x with χ(x)≠0 test divisibility. Order-p^7 analysis shows only χ(1)=p² with x of order p³ (|P|=p^6) or o(x)=p^4 (|P|=p^7) can fail, so the search is sharply targeted; a hit settles the question negatively.
- **20.115** (Wilde): χ(x)≠0 ⇒ o(x) | |G|/χ(1) (known for solvable). Attack: loop over CTblLib (all ATLAS/almost-simple/maximal-subgroup tables) and all nonsolvable SmallGroups ≤2000 + perfect groups: check every (χ, class) with χ(x)≠0. Minutes of GAP; a counterexample settles it, else a strong partial (all groups of order ≤2000 and all library tables).
- **20.78** (Qian codegree conjecture): element of order m ⇒ m divides some codegree |G:kerχ|/χ(1). Open only for nonsolvable G with F(G)≠1 and m not prime power/squarefree. Attack: all nonsolvable SmallGroups ≤2000 (e.g. 2.A5×C4, A5⋉2^4, SL(2,5)×C_n), perfect groups ≤10^6, and CTblLib tables of non-simple groups (e.g. maximal subgroups of sporadics): compute Cod(G), test every element order. Cheap; either counterexample or new verified range.
- **19.56** (Monakhov): G soluble if |ab|≥|a||b| for ⋆-commutators a,b of coprime orders. Attack: hypothesis is subgroup-hereditary, so a minimal counterexample is minimal non-soluble with G/Φ(G) minimal simple (Thompson list). Uniform arguments: in PSL(2,q) unipotents, involutions (via A4) and order-3 elements (via dihedrals) are ⋆-commutators, and (2,3,p)-generation / A4 give |ab|<|a||b|; Sz(q) via Frobenius subgroups; PSL(3,3) by GAP. Remaining gap: lifting through Φ(G) (short argument likely). Also brute-force check on all nonsolvable groups ≤2000.

Score 3
- **19.82** (Shumyatsky): does every finite G contain soluble K with h(K)=h*(G)? Attack: for all nonsolvable SmallGroups ≤2000 and perfect groups compute h*(G) and max Fitting height over soluble subgroups (via maximal soluble subgroups). Counterexample needs h* large vs. small soluble subgroups; search is cheap, may give a small counterexample.
- **20.49** (Lucchini): every finite G has a 2-generated subgroup of the same exponent (known for soluble, 3-gen always). Attack: nonsolvable SmallGroups ≤2000 and perfect groups: compute exponent, then exponent of ⟨x,y⟩ over class-representative pairs. Simple groups are 2-generated, so only non-2-generated nonsolvable groups matter — small list.
- **20.67** (Navarro): p-block B with defect group D: (a) dl(D) ≤ |cd(B)|, (b) |cd(D)| ≤ |cd(B)|. Attack: SmallGroups ≤2000 (and perfect groups), compute blocks (PrimeBlocks), defect groups via defect classes, compare with cd(D). (b) is the sharper target — non-principal blocks with few degrees are the place to look.
- **20.75/20.76** (Pyber): p-group with all abelian normal subgroups k-generated (resp. order ≤p^k) ⇒ all abelian subgroups 2k-generated (resp. ≤p^{2k}). Attack: all groups of order 2^8, 3^7, 5^6/5^7, 7^6 (2^9 partially): compute max rank/order over abelian normal vs. all abelian subgroups (via Latt/ maximal abelian subgroups). D16^k is extremal, so search around 2-groups of order 2^8–2^9.
- **20.108** (Tsang/Caranti): T(G)=NHol(G)/Hol(G): (b) finite centerless G with T(G) not elementary abelian 2-group; (c) p-group with |T(G)| having a prime divisor ∤ p(p−1). Attack: for |G|≤~200 (centerless groups, p-groups of order 2^6–2^8, 3^5, 5^4) compute T(G) as the set of regular subgroups N≅G of Hol(G) with Hol(N)=Hol(G) (Caranti's method), or Normalizer(Sym(n),Hol(G)) directly for n≤100.
- **20.122** (Zenkov): nilpotent A,B,C ≤ G: is min_G(A,B,C) ≤ F(G)? Min_G(A,B,C) ≤ F(G)? (c) same for soluble G. Attack: soluble groups of order ≤500 (then nonsoluble ≤2000), A,B,C over Sylow / maximal nilpotent subgroups, enumerate intersections A∩B^x∩C^y, take minimal ones, test containment in F(G). Small counterexamples plausible for (b)/(c).
- **20.37** (Hooshmand): |G|=ab ⇒ ∃ A,B ⊆ G, |A|=a,|B|=b, G=AB. Minimal counterexample is simple w/o prime-index subgroups. Attack: for every simple group of order ≤10^6–10^7 (via tables of marks / maximal subgroups) compute the set of "chain-achievable" pairs recursively (H<G gives (a',b'[G:H]) and ([G:H]a',b')); a simple group where some factorization is not chain-achievable is the first genuine test case (then search A,B directly there). Gives "true for all simple groups of order < X".
- **20.48** (Lewis): p-group with proper Hughes subgroup and fixed-point-free automorphism of prime order ⇒ exponent p? Attack: groups of order p^n (p=3,5,7, n≤7) with H_p(P)≠P of exponent >p (very few), compute Aut(P), search coprime prime-order fpf automorphisms. For p=2 answer is yes trivially (H_2 index 2, C_2 has no fpf automorphism). Likely confirms; may find a counterexample for p=7.
- **20.80** (Qian): G soluble iff all P-characters (constituents of 1_H^G, H maximal) are monomial; sufficiency open. Attack: nonsolvable SmallGroups ≤2000 + minimal simple groups: compute P-characters and test monomiality (subgroups of index χ(1) with linear λ, λ^G=χ). Also try to prove via minimal simple groups (Steinberg character of PSL(2,q), q>11, is non-monomial) plus reduction — partial or full.
- **19.90 b),c)** (skew braces): (b) non-soluble additive, nilpotent multiplicative; (c) soluble additive, non-soluble multiplicative. Attack: regular subgroups of Hol(A) for A nonsoluble of order ≤~1000 (SL(2,5), A5×C_n, perfect groups): test for nilpotent regular subgroups via semiregular Sylow subgroups; for (c) A soluble of order 60k-ish, search for regular subgroups ≅ A5-containing groups (e.g. A of order 120, 240, 360).
